idiom_name: app.use((req, res, next) => ...) with next() delegation
implementation_notes: Node's stdlib has no chain - http.createServer takes a single request listener - so the pattern lives in the framework: in Express the app/router is the FilterManager, the middleware stack is the FilterChain (app.use, router.use, mounted sub-stacks), a middleware is (req, res, next), and the final route handler is the target. next() is the delegation primitive, and ending the response without calling it short-circuits. Closures make the classic Filter classes unnecessary, but the registration order of app.use calls is the contract.
pitfalls: A middleware that neither ends the response nor calls next() leaves the request open until the client times out.

Errors travel only through next(err): throwing inside a plain middleware skips the error chain and crashes the process, and async handlers need a wrapper on Express 4 (Express 5 forwards rejected promises).
Registration order and mount paths decide coverage, so a mistyped mount path silently leaves routes unfiltered - and error middleware must be registered last with four parameters.

variants.name: Koa onion middleware (async/await)
variants.implementation_notes: Koa composes the same chain with promises instead of callbacks: each middleware is async (ctx, next) => { ...; await next(); ... }, the framework runs them as an onion so the code after await next() runs on the way out, and rejections propagate to the outermost error handler. The explicit next argument disappears, which removes the forgot-to-call-next class of bug but also removes route-skipping tricks such as next('route'). Koa bundles no middleware, so the chain is assembled entirely by the application.
pitfalls: A middleware that never awaits next() takes responsibility for the response; forgetting to set ctx.body then yields a 404 rather than a visible hang, which hides the bug.
Code after await next() still runs when the downstream middleware threw only if the error is handled - otherwise the rejection unwinds straight to the error middleware.
Node 18+ is required by Koa 3, and unhandled rejections outside the middleware chain terminate the process unless app.on('error') is wired.
